page: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by a 32-core Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It features a dedicated CPU allocation with one thread per core, backed by 128 MB of L3 cache. The server is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, it includes 1890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The E32pds_v6 achieves top-tier results in uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 449.0 GB/sec for read operations and 188.31 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests show strong performance, alongside top-tier database operations and strong Redis SET throughput. However, large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with 70B model prompt processing registering in the bottom 10% of benchmarks.

Utilizing ARM64 architecture, this instance offers high resource density and memory capacity, translating to qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads compared to traditional x86 alternatives. The combination of 256 GB of RAM, dedicated physical cores, and fast local NVMe storage makes the E32pds_v6 highly suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, high-throughput web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
